title: Qualify Emojineer 1.0 release readiness
description: Freeze feature work and prove the complete 1.0 product from installation through real projects, compatibility, malformed input, and cross-platform operation.
acceptance_criteria: Grammar and compatibility policy are frozen/documented; old supported EMJBC/package artifacts are exercised; lexer/parser/bytecode/EASM/package/registry readers have fuzz or hostile-input coverage; Windows/Linux/macOS clean-install journeys pass; editor, playground, web markup, packages, debugger, capabilities, and representative apps pass release-candidate acceptance; release notes and upgrade guidance are complete; the project has an explicit release-license decision and packaged editor/distribution metadata matches that decision.
notes:
VSIX packaging currently warns because the repository has no tracked license file; do not invent a license. Resolve explicitly before 1.0 release.
macOS PR matrix exposed canonical-path aliasing (/var -> /private/var): registry/package source containment compared canonical child paths to a non-canonical package root, producing false symlink-escape rejections across package/project/module/LSP acceptance. Fixed hashing boundaries to canonicalize roots before traversal/containment/relative paths and added a non-Windows directory-symlink alias regression. WSL Debug full CTest remains 32/32 green.
Second macOS matrix pass reduced failures from five to two and isolated the remaining issue to package-graph root identity: pkg import confinement and ownership compared canonical imported paths against non-canonical resolved package roots. Resolver::visit now canonicalizes every package root at graph entry, preserving escape checks while normalizing ownership/import identity. Targeted package/module/Train 15 acceptance tests pass; full WSL Debug CTest 32/32 green.
Third macOS matrix pass proved runtime/package behavior but exposed two non-portable test expectations that compared canonical production paths against aliased temp path spellings. Updated package-root and SourceLocationException path assertions to compare canonical identities; no runtime/security relaxation. Targeted package/module tests and full WSL Debug CTest 32/32 green.
Windows release precedent exposed three POSIX-only implicit filesystem path/string conversions in lock/store metadata. Replaced them with explicit generic_string()/filesystem::path conversions. Verified src/project.cpp with local Windows MinGW-w64 C++20 syntax check and full WSL Debug CTest 32/32 green.

title: Design and build Emojineer-native web markup
description: Add a webpage authoring layer where Emojineer source is the markup itself, not front matter around HTML. Define a typed document/DOM IR first, then a native emoji grammar that lowers to semantic accessible web output; interactive behavior uses explicit browser host ABI surfaces.
acceptance_criteria: Emojineer can author headings, sections, navigation, images, links, buttons, forms, lists, tables, and styling through native source; output uses semantic accessible HTML/DOM; the document IR is inspectable/testable; interactive behavior does not secretly become a second JavaScript language; browser playground can render the examples.
close_reason: Native .emjweb grammar, typed WebDocument/WebNode IR, semantic accessible HTML lowering, safe styling/URL boundaries, explicit browser bindings, sandboxed production-VM behavior exports, CLI authoring surfaces, and playground rendering implemented. WSL Debug suite 31/31 green; Emscripten 6.0.5 WASM smoke passes web render/behavior/hostile-markup plus Unicode parity.

title: Deliver the browser playground and universal try-it path
description: Provide a no-install browser path that executes real Emojineer semantics rather than a JavaScript reimplementation. Reuse the sovereign compiler/runtime and Train 21/22 boundaries deliberately.
acceptance_criteria: A user can open a static or hosted playground, edit native .emoji source, run it in a sandbox, see stdout/diagnostics, load curated examples, and share a reproducible source link or payload; browser execution cannot gain ambient host authority; VM/browser equivalence tests cover representative programs.
close_reason: Static browser playground now runs the real Emojineer compiler+VM as Emscripten WebAssembly with pinned ICU data, permanent sandbox authority, curated examples/share links, native equivalence tests, and real WASM smoke green.

title: Build the five-minute tour, templates, and real example corpus
description: Replace reference-doc-only onboarding with a progressive user journey and representative projects.
acceptance_criteria: A new user can follow Install -> five-minute tour -> first project -> package use -> language reference; emji init offers useful templates; examples include calculator/game, text or data processing, CLI utility, package use, network/capability use, CER, interop, and EASM; examples are executable acceptance fixtures where practical.
close_reason: Five-minute tour, four emji init templates, representative executable example corpus, package/capability/CER/interop/EASM journeys implemented; WSL Debug full suite 30/30 green on current working tree based on a6da37a8fe2745959f06f0122d5f39c1cb72dcd2.

title: Add first-class bytes and encoding utilities
description: Make encoding a practical Emojineer domain. Provide a coherent bytes/text boundary and explicit codecs while preserving grapheme-aware source semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Programs can represent bounded byte sequences and explicitly encode/decode documented text/binary formats through ordinary language/stdlib APIs; UTF-8 behavior and malformed-input handling are specified; round-trip and boundary tests cover Unicode/grapheme edge cases. This does not implement Emoji Stories or secret-note codecs.
close_reason: Bounded first-class bytes plus explicit UTF-8, hex, and Base64 codecs are implemented with malformed UTF-8, non-canonical Base64, byte-vs-grapheme boundary, round-trip, byte indexing/update, module-linking, EMJBC v10, Debug/Release 27/27, and ASan/UBSan coverage green. Emoji Stories remain out of scope.

title: Close practical CLI and host-I/O gaps
description: Make capability-gated Emojineer suitable for ordinary utilities and automation. Extend the existing authority model rather than adding ambient access.
acceptance_criteria: A normal program can receive command-line arguments and perform a documented minimum set of capability-gated filesystem write/directory and richer network request operations needed by real CLI utilities; denial remains preflighted/default-deny where applicable; deterministic/sandbox modes remain truthful; end-to-end utility examples pass.
close_reason: Explicit run/exec argv plus default-deny capability-gated filesystem write/directory and bounded richer HTTPS request facilities are implemented. Preflight denial proves zero filesystem effects; sandbox/deterministic policy, linked-module authority, utility CLI/runtime tests, Debug/Release 27/27, and ASan/UBSan qualification are green.

title: Close practical application data-model gaps
description: Add the minimum boring data-model features needed for useful non-demo programs without creating a second dialect. Audit and implement the smallest coherent set around user records or structures, key-value data, and richer explicit error/result values.
acceptance_criteria: Representative structured-data programs can model named records, keyed values, and recoverable failures using documented ordinary Emojineer semantics; parser/compiler/VM/bytecode/tooling/package behavior is covered by compatibility and regression tests.
close_reason: Named records, keyed values, and recoverable result values are implemented as ordinary verifier-visible Emojineer semantics. Module/package linking preserves pure intrinsics; EMJBC v10 compatibility/fencing, LSP/editor exposure, ABI rejection behavior, Debug/Release 27/27, and ASan/UBSan qualification are green.

title: Package the Emojineer editor experience
description: Turn the existing sovereign LSP into an installable editor experience, starting with VS Code/Cursor-compatible packaging. Make native emoji source easy to enter without replacing it with an ASCII dialect.
acceptance_criteria: An installable extension launches or locates emojineer-lsp, provides syntax/semantic presentation, run/check/fmt/debug commands, and a searchable semantic palette that inserts canonical emoji tokens; accessibility text is available; workspace/package behavior still uses the production LSP/compiler model.
close_reason: VS Code/Cursor extension packages production LSP, run/check/fmt/debug commands and semantic emoji palette; npm validation and VSIX packaging green

title: Ship installable cross-platform Emojineer distributions
description: Create the distribution/release layer around emojineer, emji, and emojineer-lsp so users do not need a local C++ toolchain merely to try the language.
acceptance_criteria: Versioned Windows, Linux, and macOS artifacts are produced by repeatable release automation; Windows has a first-class portable/install path; artifacts carry checksums and release metadata; clean-machine install, PATH, version, run, and uninstall/cleanup smoke tests exist; signing hooks are supported without requiring secrets for local qualification.
close_reason: Cross-platform CPack/release automation, install layout, Windows portable install/uninstall, version identity, checksums and installed-tool smoke implemented and locally qualified

title: Define the Emojineer 1.0 product contract and domain boundary
description: Define the 1.0 target user journey and release contract. Universal distribution, encoding/bytes, browser execution, and Emojineer-native web markup are 1.0-track concerns. Retro profiles/targets remain future domain work unless required for portability. Emoji Stories and breakable physical-note secret-code schemes are explicitly reserved for 2.0/post-1.0 and must not leak into the first release.
acceptance_criteria: A versioned product-contract document states install-to-first-program goals, supported platforms, compatibility promises, 1.0 in-scope domains, explicit non-goals, and the 2.0 Emoji Stories reservation; roadmap language agrees with it.
close_reason: 1.0 product/domain contract documented and roadmap aligned

title: Emojineer 1.0 productization arc
description: Turn the post-0.22 language engine into a product a new user can install, learn, use, share, and trust. Covers distribution, editor UX, practical application gaps, encoding, browser use, native Emojineer web markup, and 1.0 hardening.
acceptance_criteria: All child beads are closed; the hardening capstone proves the documented 1.0 user journey and compatibility contract; post-1.0 domain ideas remain explicitly out of scope.
